author: opencode-worker-5
text: DESIGN DECISIONS RESOLVED (survey 2026-08-31, evidence-based — implementation is now unblocked): (1) Schnorr48 verify = lichen-link::schnorr (re-exports the vetted crates.io schnorr48 crate: derive_keypair/sign/verify; lichen-rpl already has dep:lichen-link under its std feature — no oscore involvement; the signed message is SHA256(COSE Sig_structure) per the vectors' signature_input, and the COSE 'Signature1' context IS the domain separation so raw verify applies, no extra prefix). (2) AddrForKey dodagid binding = SHA-512 derivation; wire-compatible precedents already in-repo at lichen-core/src/addr.rs:73,97 and lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs:487 (documented as matching Yggdrasil AddrForKey) — implement in the verify module with sha2::Sha512 (lichen-rpl already deps sha2 under std), citing those references. (3) CBOR = ciborium 0.2 — the repo's OWN established choice (lichen-cli:21, lichen-client:18, lichen-gateway:28 all pin ciborium='0.2'; already in Cargo.lock so zero new supply-chain surface), no_std-compatible, COSE-native. Remaining implementation outline: decode cose_sign1 (tag 18 array(4)), check protected alg==-65537 + kid==source IID, rebuild sig_structure ['Signature1', protected, b'', payload], sha256, schnorr48::verify, dodagid==AddrForKey(pubkey), expiry vs current_time, DIO field cross-checks, then RootSeqCache.accept — driven by all 14 cases of test/vectors/root_dio_signature.json. Feature-gate: std (where lichen-link is available). Releasing per TIMEBOX — decisions recorded here so implementation can be a clean follow-on round.
